description.text: ICON is a global provider of outsourced development and commercialization services to pharmaceutical, biotechnology, medical device, and government and public health organizations. We offer a full range of clinical, consulting and commercial services that range from clinical development strategy, planning and trial design, to full study execution, and post-market commercialization. ICON provides its services across a range of clinical outsourcing operating models including strategic partnerships, preferred provider, full-service delivery to functional service provision and stand-alone services. We specialize in the strategic development, management and analysis of programs that support all stages of the clinical development process, from compound selection to Phase I-IV clinical studies. We earn revenue by providing a number of different services to our customers. These services are integral components of the clinical development process and include clinical trial management, consulting, contract staffing, data solutions and laboratory services. Our vision is to be the partner of choice by delivering industry leading solutions and best in class performance in clinical development.

about.description_short: ICON plc is a world-leading clinical research organization. Offering deep operational and medical expertise we accelerate innovation, driving emerging therapies forward to improve patient outcomes. From molecule to medicine, we deliver integrated consulting, clinical development, commercialization and post-marketing solutions to pharmaceutical, biotechnology, medical device, government and public health organizations worldwide. With headquarters in Dublin, Ireland, ICON employed approximately 40,200 employees in 99 locations in 55 countries as at June 30, 2026.

analysis_md:
# ICLR — ICON plc
Engine 5.4.0 run, 2026-10-18. All figures below are copied from dcf_numbers.json, financials_history.csv or fundamentals.json — none are recomputed.

## What it is
Dublin-based contract research organisation (CRO): one of the two largest global providers of outsourced clinical development to pharma, biotech, medical-device and government sponsors — trial design and management, labs, site networks, data/biostatistics, pharmacovigilance and functional-service-provider (FSP) embedding. Revenue FY2025 $8,251,340,000, nearly flat on FY2024 ($8,188,990,000, +0.8% latest YoY in dcf_numbers.json). Backlog $21.8B at December 31, 2025 under the new backlog policy and $23.4B at June 30, 2026 (company releases). Market cap $13.44B at the $170.18 price (nasdaq_quote_api) — in scope under $40B.

## Owner's earnings
**FY2025 (20-F via EDGAR, from financials_history.csv):** operating cash flow $1,036,205,000; capex $174,214,000; SBC $102,041,000 (always a real cost — and note it more than doubled from $45,870,000 in FY2024).
- **Conservative owner's earnings FY2025: $759,950,000 = $9.62/share** (base_oe_latest_per_share in dcf_numbers.json)
- Maintenance version (NI + D&A − min(capex, D&A) − ΔNWC): $880,807,000 — same ballpark; the OCF-based figure is used throughout because FY2025 net income ($229,339,000) carries $364,248,000 of goodwill impairment and $101,027,000 of impairment of non-financial assets (20-F consolidated statements of operations), both non-cash.
- OE positive 5 of the last 5 fiscal years. Net debt $2,225,321,000 (dcf_numbers.json, LongTermDebtNoncurrent basis; cash $647,295,000), plus lease liabilities $153,404,000 — 2.42x normalised OE. The company reported net debt of $2.5B at June 30, 2026, 1.8x adjusted EBITDA.
- Buybacks: $750M of stock repurchased in FY2025 at an average $167/share (company release); diluted shares fell from 83,032,424 (FY2024) to 78,965,385 (FY2025), share CAGR −1.44%/yr, which the engine credits only to the revenue growth components.

**Base used = median of the last 3 fiscal years' OE/share, $11.66/share** (base_source: median_of_last_3_fy_oe_per_share; the three years are $11.66 FY2023, $12.92 FY2024, $9.62 FY2025). This is a 20-F filer and ttm.py cannot build a TTM pin for it (it exited non-zero: no us-gaap annual facts on its timeline), so per the worker spec the median base is used and the run-rate gap is handled in the scenario multipliers instead (below). Cross-check from fundamentals.json: its filing-direct TTM through June 30, 2026 shows OE of $761,105,000, OE/share $9.82, on revenue of $8,330,136,000 — the current run rate sits ~16% below the median base, which is exactly why the base-case OE multiplier is 0.90 (effective starting OE $10.49/share) and the bear multiplier 0.80 lands on the current run rate.

## Moat: 5/10 — moderate/narrow, scale-based
Justification: one of the few CROs that can run a global late-phase programme, mid-trial switching costs, and a $21.8B backlog — but measured returns since the PRA deal sit below the cost of capital, gross margin is thin, sponsors hold the pricing power, and the 2025–26 revenue-recognition restatement damaged trust.
- FOR: scale (top-two global CRO, ~$8.25B revenue, $21.8B backlog at Dec 2025 rising to $23.4B at Jun 2026); mid-trial switching costs are real — replacing a CRO mid-study risks timelines, data continuity and regulatory filings; strategic partnerships and FSP embedding inside large pharma; structurally strong cash conversion (OE positive 5/5 years; FY2025 OCF $1,036M vs capex of only $174M).
- AGAINST: return history — roic_proxy (fundamentals.json) was 25.2% in FY2020 pre-deal, then 2.4% (FY2021), 5.5% (FY2022), 7.0% (FY2023), 7.7% (FY2024) and 3.5% (FY2025) after the $12B PRA Health acquisition; gross margin ~29% for FY2020–24 (29.2 / 27.5 / 28.6 / 29.0 / 28.6 in fundamentals.json) with FY2025 direct costs of $6,075,746,000 rising against nearly flat revenue; cancellations are structural (FY2025 cancellations $2,834M under the new policy; backlog itself was cut $3.9B by a policy change to $21.1B at October 1, 2025); contested oligopoly (IQVIA, Thermo Fisher/PPD, Medpace); the Audit Committee investigation found improper revenue-timing adjustments overstating FY2023 revenue by $65M and FY2024 by $93M, with material weaknesses in internal controls still being remediated through 2026.
- A 5 gives CAP = 8.5 years: growth holds 2 years, then converges linearly to the 2.5% terminal rate over 8.5 years, 15-year projection. A moat of 7+ would need ROIC sustained well above the cost of capital through a cycle; ICON's post-2021 history shows the opposite.

## DCF — final run (2026-10-18)
**Growth sanity check (mandatory):** the engine's blended start is 2.89%, but its components straddle the PRA break (5-yr revenue CAGR 24.16% is a deal artefact; 3-yr CAGR 2.15%, latest YoY 0.76%, OE/share CAGR −9.15%). Actual recent prints: FY2025 revenue +0.8%, Q1 2026 +0.9%, Q2 2026 +1.2%, and management guides FY2026 revenue to $7,850–8,150M — a down year versus $8,251M in FY2025 — with adjusted EPS guided to $10.00–11.00 versus $12.53 adjusted in FY2025. Scenario starts were therefore recalibrated with offsets −0.11 / −0.06 / −0.03 / +0.01 / +0.05 against the blend, to −8.1% / −3.1% / −0.1% / +3.9% / +7.9%: the base case starts where the guidance is, not where the blend sits, and even the super-bull start (7.9%) is a re-acceleration claim, not an extrapolation. OE multipliers were also shifted down from the defaults (0.65 / 0.80 / 0.90 / 1.00 / 1.15) because the $11.66 median base sits above the $9.62 latest-FY and $9.82 TTM run rates (see Owner's earnings). Probabilities 15/30/30/15/10 put 45% on bear-or-worse, reflecting the guided down year, the control remediation overhang and elevated cancellations. Price $170.18.

| Scenario | Prob | Growth start | OE mult | Story | IV@15 | IRR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Super bear | 15% | −8.1% | 0.65 | Cancellations bite, direct-cost pressure persists, controls remediation drags | $39.86 | 5.08% |
| Bear | 30% | −3.1% | 0.80 | The guided 2026 decline happens and recovery is slow; OE stays at the current run rate | $60.52 | 6.72% |
| Base | 30% | −0.1% | 0.90 | Flat start on partial recovery toward the median base, then terminal fade | $77.19 | 8.07% |
| Bull | 15% | 3.9% | 1.00 | Book-to-bill strength (1.42 in Q1 2026, 1.51 in Q2 2026) converts; OE back to the median | $101.33 | 9.99% |
| Super bull | 10% | 7.9% | 1.15 | Biotech funding recovery plus backlog conversion drives high-single-digit growth | $137.53 | 12.71% |

- **Probability-weighted: IV@15% $76.24 (−55.2% vs price), IV@12% $99.82, IV@10% $125.95, weighted IRR 8.03%, base-case IRR 8.07%**
- **Tier by numbers: D** (bear D, bull D — no tier band). Diagnostics (dcf_numbers.json): OE yield 6.85%, terminal value 17.3% of IV@15%, scenario spread 3.45x, net debt 2.42x normalised OE, 9.6 months since FY end.
- ADS basis: ads_ratio 1.0 applied — the 20-F cover registers the ordinary shares themselves (par €0.06, symbol ICLR, Nasdaq), so per-share figures and the traded price are on the same basis; recorded in judgment.json under the bounded filing authority.

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
- **STALE_FY** (FY ended 9.6 months ago): ttm.py cannot compute a pin for this 20-F filer (exited non-zero — no us-gaap annual facts on its timeline), so the median base is used per spec. The gap is not ignored: fundamentals.json's filing-direct TTM through Q2 2026 (OE/share $9.82) sits below the median base, and that is handled by shifting the OE multipliers down rather than by pinning a base the tools did not produce.
- **BASIS_BREAK_SUSPECT**: the PRA Health Sciences acquisition ($12B, closed July 2021). Revenue went $2,797,288,000 (FY2020) → $5,480,826,000 (FY2021) → $7,741,386,000 (FY2022) and diluted shares 53,283,585 → 68,068,311 → 82,468,363. Every CAGR straddling 2021 is a deal artefact; growth inputs were set from post-deal prints and 2026 guidance only. The FY2023/FY2024 figures in the history are the restated ones (revenue overstated by $65M / $93M in the original filings).
- **OE_VOLATILE** (OE/share spans >3x over 5 years: $8.84, $4.25, $11.66, $12.92, $9.62 for FY2021–25): the FY2022 trough is the first full PRA year (share count up ~55% on FY2020 while OCF dipped to $563,315,000); the FY2025 step-down is margin compression plus SBC doubling. Handled with the normalised median base and 45% probability on bear-or-worse.
- **NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE** (2023, 2024, 2025): D&A explains the bulk each year — $585,950,000 / $488,500,000 / $382,996,000 of mostly PRA intangible amortisation sits in net income but not OCF. FY2025 adds the $364,248,000 goodwill impairment (Data Solutions reporting unit) and $101,027,000 impairment of non-financial assets, both non-cash. The OCF-based conservative OE used throughout is clean of all of it; no tax-deposit or working-capital one-off is driving the base.
- **ADS_RATIO_APPLIED** (x1.0): see the ADS basis note above — direct-listed ordinary shares, source cited in judgment.json.
- Preliminary-run flags that the recalibration resolved: **WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD** (4.52x on default assumptions → 3.45x final; confidence is low in any case) and **TIER_BAND** (preliminary bear D vs bull C → final all-D; the verdict no longer spans tiers).

## My thoughts / overlay
- The honest headline is the method range: the preliminary default run (median base, default multipliers and probabilities) printed weighted IRR 10.24% and IV@15% $104.13 (Tier C); the recalibrated final run prints 8.03% (Tier D). Both sit far below the $170.18 price — the disagreement is over how overvalued it is, not whether it is.
- What the market is paying for is the adjusted story (FY2025 adjusted EPS $12.53, adjusted EBITDA $1,530.7M at 18.6% of revenue). On filed owner's earnings the cash yield is 6.85% at a business whose revenue is guided down, whose largest recent profit year is two years old, and whose controls are under remediation. Even the super-bull case — 7.9% growth start, OE at 1.15x the median base — returns only 12.71%: at this price there is no scenario in the model that clears Andrew's 15% hurdle.
- Cash generation is genuinely not the problem: TTM OCF of $1,070,040,000 (fundamentals.json) through Q2 2026, buybacks running, backlog rebuilding ($22.7B at Q1 2026, $23.4B at Q2 2026) on book-to-bill above 1.4. If the price fell toward the weighted IV the quality question would be worth re-arguing; at $170 it is a price question, and the price is wrong for a 15% hurdle.
- Balance-sheet risk is modest, not negligible: net debt 2.42x normalised OE, and the PRA goodwill pile is still being written down ($364M in FY2025) — further impairments would hit reported earnings, not the OE base.

## Final verdict
- **Final tier: D** (weighted IRR 8.03% on the final inputs; method range C to D across the day's defensible runs, both far below the price)
- Confidence: **Low** (restatement and material weaknesses still remediating, volatile OE history, guided down year — the direction of the verdict is not in doubt, the exact IRR is)
- One-liner: Scale CRO with a narrow moat 5/10 and post-PRA returns below the cost of capital — does not clear 15% at $170.18 (weighted IRR 8.0%, IV@15% $76.24 vs $170.18 price); even the super-bull case returns only 12.7%, and 2026 is guided down — clears 15% only below ~$76.
